comments:
The NASA Small Business Program, grounded in the Small Business Act and statutorily focused on 51 U.S.C. §20113(e), champions the extraordinary contributions small businesses make to NASA’s mission.  As the gateway for many companies entering the NASA ecosystem, the NASA Small Business Program ensures that small firms thrive within one of the most innovative and demanding procurement environments in the world.  NASA’s ambitious work of returning humans to the lunar surface, building a sustainable presence, and maturing the technologies that will carry humanity deeper into the solar system creates unique challenges for small companies, and the NASA Small Business Program plays a critical role supporting their participation in NASA contracts to keep the agency at the forefront of science, aeronautics, and space exploration.
 In fiscal year 2025, more than 1,500 small businesses performed NASA prime contracts—an extraordinary indicator of their impact.  NASA exceeded many of its small business goals, including its small business prime contracts goal, where achievements were at the highest level in a decade.  Altogether, small businesses earned over $7 billion in NASA prime and subcontract awards, underscoring their essential role in every major mission NASA undertakes.   Small businesses continue to deliver ingenuity, speed, and specialized capabilities that propel advances across NASA’s science, technology, and human exploration portfolios.

comments: The Department of Justice (DOJ) is thankful for the contributions of the small business contractors that supported the department’s critical missions in fiscal year (FY) 2025.  FY 2025 marks the twelfth consecutive fiscal year that DOJ achieved an “A” on SBA’s Small Business Procurement Scorecard.  DOJ recognizes the vital role that American small businesses have in the important work of the Department of Justice, and it renews its commitment to support small businesses in FY 2026. Further, DOJ looks forward to continuing its collaboration with SBA toward the shared goal of increasing opportunities for small businesses.

comments: The Department of the Interior is honored to receive an A on our FY 2025 small business scorecard and proud to have earned an A or A+ for 17 consecutive years. In FY 2025, small businesses provided more than $2.9 billion in products and services to support Interior’s programs, representing over 57% of our contract obligations. The Department exceeded its overall small business prime contracting goal but did not meet the Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business prime contracting goal. Looking ahead to FY 2026, Interior is committed to strengthening our support for veterans through increased engagement with the Department of Veterans Affairs and the Small Business Administration’s Office of Veterans Business Development. We will continue building on our strong track record and advancing our program to ensure meaningful opportunities for small businesses.

comments: The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) is honored to receive an annual procurement scorecard rating of "A+", from the Small Business Administration (SBA).  The recognition represents significant accomplishments made by HUD to create contracting opportunities for small business concerns in all categories and acknowledges the many small businesses across the country that assist HUD in achieving its mission and contribute to its culture of excellence.  In FY 2025, HUD exceeded all of its annual small business prime goals.  This achievement was due to the collaborative efforts of the program offices, procurement, OSDBU staff, and the Department's senior leadership.  HUD conducted outreach events and training sessions to increase awareness of contracting opportunities at HUD and throughout the federal marketplace.  HUD remains committed to educating its acquisition workforce and clients on changes in acquisition policies and regulations that impact small business utilization and programs.  With its robust acquisition planning processes, the Department is committed to empowering America’s entrepreneurs and job creators and will continue to identify areas to maximize practicable opportunities for small businesses in both prime and subcontracting opportunities.

comments:
The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) remains fully committed to supporting its mission and operations through acquisitions with small businesses to drive innovation, optimize efficiency and cost savings, and grow the domestic supplier industrial base. All of which contributes to the agency achieving its statutorily mandated small business economic goals and entrepreneurial targets. 
The NRC's Small Business Program has implemented a compliance, technical assistance, and training program designed to maximize prime and subcontract opportunities for small businesses and entrepreneurs. The interdependency and collaboration between the Small Business Program, purchasing offices, and the agency’s acquisition team throughout the acquisition planning and market research stages of procurement was vital towards driving success. As a result, the agency exceeded four out of five of its small business prime contract economic goals, nearly achieving its 43 percent small business goal, which we missed by less than one percent. The NRC is proud that it exceeded its Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business goal in fiscal year 2025 following the implementation of a remedial action plan, after previously falling short of the target in fiscal year 2024.
The agency remains dedicated to driving transformative small business growth by leveraging strategic initiatives and fulfilling Small Business Program legislatively mandated responsibilities. Moving forward, the Small Business Program will continue to implement targeted activities to identify efficiencies and cost saving measures, refine agency resources, enhance market research analysis, and apply innovative procurement practices to promote competition and strengthen the domestic industrial base.
